description:
FILED s463f (Fable, 2026-09-01) from a USER question during the #930 discussion ("won't a lot of normal subs return values that are lvalue style and modify variables when they shouldn't?") -- the answer was measured, and it is YES, TODAY, independent of #930.

PERL'S RULE: a non-lvalue sub returns a mortal COPY of each returned value (pp_leavesub); only a `:lvalue` sub returns the variable itself.

PCL TODAY (main 6e6f191, probes scratchpad probes/leak.pl + leak2.pl of session 16e00e26; perl 5.40.3 answers 1 for every row):
    my $x = 1; sub f { $x }  sub fr { return $x }
    for my $v (f())  { $v = 5 }        x=5   (perl 1)
    for my $v (fr()) { $v = 5 }        x=5
    $_ = 7 for f();                      x=7
    my @m = map { $_ = 8 } f();         x=8
    my @g = grep { $_ = 9 } f();        x=9
    my $r = \f(); $$r = 10;            x=10  (also \fr())
    sub mod { $_[0] = 12 } mod(f());     x=12
    for (st()) { s/a/Z/ }                 s=Z   (a string var through a foreach alias)
    our $g; sub fg { $g } for (fg()) { $_ = 7 }   g=7  (package variables too)
  and the shapes that do NOT leak:
    sub g { $h{k} } / sub h { $a[0] }    elements come back RAW (the s455 boxed-aggregates model copies)
    sub arg { $_[0] }                      the argbox path copies
    sub sh { my $t = shift; $t }          a sub-local my (nobody else holds it)
  The leak is the SAME under the default optimizer and PCL_OPT=none, and the same for a numeric-verdict name -- so it is the return PROTOCOL, not a regime.

WHERE: the emission is `(p-sub pl-f (&rest %_args) (p-args-body (block nil $x)))` -- the tail expression IS the box; `p-return` likewise hands the box through.  Nothing copies at the return site, and the consumers cannot tell a returned box from any other box.

DESIGN NOTE -- THIS AND #930 ARE ONE RETURN POLICY: perl's is "copy unless :lvalue"; PCL's today is "always the box" (which is why #930's shape s1 'works' by accident and every other :lvalue shape misses).  The fix for both is the same switch at the return site (tail + every `return`): an ordinary sub returns a COPY of a box-valued scalar (raw values are already copies), a `:lvalue` sub returns the place.  Do NOT fix this at the consumers (foreach/map/grep/\/argbox) -- that is N copies of one rule (CLAUDE.md 11) and misses the next consumer.  Interaction with #77 (return-family transfer, round 18): the copy is the value the transfer carries; measure that they compose.

COST BAR (USER asked, s463f): the copy is one box allocation per boxed-scalar return, exactly perl's mortalcopy; raw-verdict returns (fib, counting loops) already return values and must emit IDENTICAL code.  fib(27), ovlsub, the OO-entry row and intloop rows unchanged within noise, PCL absolute seconds compared.  If a copy per boxed return shows on a row, the escape is a copy-on-ALIAS at the return site keyed on whether the returned name ESCAPES (it is a my that dies with the frame -> no copy), which is a VarAnnotator fact.

BAR: the rows above vs perl on both emission paths; the two non-leaking families unmoved; corpus-diff + emission-ab (an emission change) + gen bump; full sweep (every sub return); companion op/sub.t + op/lvref.t legs; guard rows inverse-verified.

SCHEDULING: round 21, TOGETHER with #930's scalar half as one owner of the return family (they are the same switch) -- not in a round where the perf slot owns VarAnnotator/sub lowering.

IS IT TESTED? (USER asked, s463f)  Perl's own t/op/sub.t has the [perl #91844] "return should always copy" block (rows 4-10): six rows pass on PCL by ACCIDENT (a delete() result is a fresh value) and ROW 9 `isnt \sub { ()=\@_; shift }->($x), \$x, 'result of shift is copied when returned'` FAILS -- it is inside the blessed DIFF snapshot op/sub.t 53/12 (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv) and had never been attributed to the return protocol.  It is this task's ONE visible row in the suites; the plain `sub f { $x }` shape is not tested by perl's suite at all (its copy rows all go through delete/shift), and no Pl/t guard covers it.  Expected mover when fixed: op/sub.t 53/12 -> 54/11.  The perl-tests/ sweep copy of sub.t is the older extraction and lacks the block.

THE Pl/t GUARD IS VACUOUS: Pl/t/foreach-aliasing-01.t:103 `for(f()) does not write back (normal sub returns a copy)` uses `sub f { my $v=7; return $v }` -- the sub-LOCAL my, the one shape where the copy is unobservable -- and asserts only that the program prints "ok".  It cannot fail on this bug.  The fix must REPLACE it with the observable shape (an outer `my $x` returned and then written through the alias, asserting $x) under the s377 four-conjunct rule, and add the map/grep/\f()/@_-writer spellings.
=== DESIGN (Fable, s464, 2026-09-02) â THE RETURN PROTOCOL, MEASURED AND SIZED ===

MEASURED on main a8b4043 (probe scratchpad p964/leak.pl, 38 rows, perl 5.40.3 oracle;
IDENTICAL under PCL_OPT=none): 24 of 38 rows leak.  Leaking: the tail forms `$x`,
`$x || $s`, `do { $x }`, `($x,$s)`, `@a`, `@_`, `shift`, `our $g`, `$_`, a string var
through s///, an anon sub (both `sub {â¦}->()` and a closure), `&f()`, `goto &f`, a
string-eval-defined sub, `$_[0]` returned from a method (`\$o->self`), and BOTH
`return @a` and `return ($x,$s)` â the latter copied the NUMBER and aliased the
STRING (p-return-value's container arm tests `(vectorp v)`, and a CL string is a
vector, so a string-holding box is returned intact).  Not leaking: `return $x`
(p-return-value unboxes a plain scalar), the ternary tail, sub-local `my`, raw
elements (`$a[0]`, `$r->{k}`), `my $self = shift; $self`, and the str-buffer rows
(`.=` on either side after a copy).  perl copies at BOTH sub and eval-BLOCK exit
(pp_leavesub / pp_leaveeval: `for (eval { $x }) { $_ = 5 }` leaves $x = 1) and NOT at
`do { }` (`\do { $x }` IS \$x) â the eval frame is a SIBLING rule, out of this
task's scope: file it.

THE ONE MECHANISM.  A runtime function `%p-leavesub (v)` = perl's leave rule applied
to the VALUE of a sub frame at its exit, reading the caller's context (`*wantarray*`
is still the caller's at that point; p-sub binds *pcl-caller-wantarray* FROM it and
never rebinds it):
  :void  -> v unchanged (nothing consumes it).
  scalar -> a p-box: PLAIN (no is-ref, no class, value not a hash-table / non-string
            vector / function) -> (unbox v), nil -> *p-undef* â exactly p-return-value's
            last arm; the raw value IS the copy, zero allocation.  Ref / blessed /
            container box -> a FRESH box with the same value, is-ref and class â
            p-copy-scalar-arg's body: REUSE it (rename or call), never a second copy.
            A non-box -> unchanged (an array's vector stays for the consumer to count,
            as the tail form does today).
  list   -> a box: the scalar rule (one element; nil -> *p-undef* so it does not
            vanish from the list).  A non-string vector -> a FRESH adjustable
            fill-pointer vector (p-flatten-args' shape) with the scalar rule applied
            per element: box elements (`(vector $x $s)` temps, elem-cells / defelem
            boxes of a previously flattened array, `@_`'s caller boxes) unbox or copy,
            raw elements pass.  NEVER in place: `&f;` and `goto &f` SHARE @_ with the
            caller, so a vector reaching the exit may be someone else's.  A hash-table
            or other raw value -> unchanged (the consumer flattens k/v fresh).
  Cost = perl's: raw returns (fib, gcdrec, collatz) pay one special read + one struct
  typep; plain boxed scalars pay nothing (unbox); `$self` pays one box; a list return
  pays one vector + per element, which is pp_leavesub's own per-SV mortalcopy.

THE SITES â ONE SPELLING: a runtime macro `p-sub-frame (&body)` =
`(%p-leavesub (catch :p-return ,@body))`, used by p-sub and EMITTED by the anon-sub
wrapper at its three sites (Parser2 _lower_embedded_anon x2 ~10553/10613, Parser.pm
6037/6136 v1 seam) in place of the bare `(catch :p-return â¦)`.  NOT sites: p-sort-cmp
(the comparator value is numified), p-eval-block / the string-eval catch (eval frames,
the sibling rule above), p-goto-sub (the target's own frame copies).  p-return stays
(its list flattening and *wantarray* rebind are still needed); its p-return-value
container arm gets `(not (stringp v))` in the same commit.  #930 later: an `:lvalue` sub
is emitted with a frame that OMITS the copy â this macro is the switch; do not
implement it here, a one-line comment.

BENCH BAR (USER): `perl tools/bench-exec.pl` ALL rows best-of-5, main vs branch on the
same quiet machine; raw-return rows (gcdrec, collatz, intloop) and ovlsub / symref /
arrhash within noise.  If a row moves beyond noise, the escape is compile-time, keyed on
_sub_return_facts: a sub whose every return is a proven raw expression gets a frame
without the copy â a named Kind-A entry in Pl/Passes.pm, since PCL_OPT=none must run
identically.

GUARDS: replace the vacuous foreach-aliasing-01.t:103 row with the observable shape
(outer `my $x` returned, written through the alias, $x asserted); new
Pl/t/return-copy-01.t = the 38-row battery in ~4 programs (one `is` per program
against perl's text; measure with `prove --timer`), INVERSE-VERIFIED on a main
worktree (the 24 leaking rows must fail there).

=== s464a RESULT (Opus, 2026-09-02) â SHIPPED on branch worktree-agent-a9203dffcad74e505, commit 782d739 (base a8b4043).  status stays `pending` for Fable's review. ===

WHAT SHIPPED.  ONE runtime rule at ONE place: %p-leavesub (+ %p-leavesub-scalar
/ %p-leavesub-vector / %p-leavesub-aggregate), reached through a macro
`p-sub-frame` = `(%p-leavesub (catch :p-return â¦))`.  p-sub expands to it; the
anon-sub wrapper EMITS it at its three sites (Pl/Parser2.pm
_lower_embedded_anon x2, Pl/Parser.pm's v1 seam x1).  NOT sites: p-sort-cmp,
p-eval-block / the string-eval catch (-> #987), p-goto-sub.  p-return-value's
container arm gained `(not (stringp v))` AND an explicit dualvar arm (below).
Exports: p-sub-frame.  Normative text: docs/ir-spec.md Â§5.3, rewritten (Â§5.1
item 4 too).  Generation v2-590; all three checked-in artifacts regenerated.

PROBES.  scratch p964/leak.pl, 38 rows: BEFORE 24 rows leaked (identically
under PCL_OPT=none); AFTER byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 on BOTH emission
paths.  A second battery (leak2.pl, 20 rows: referent sharing through the copy,
push-then-write, list assign, wantarray, overload identity, sort, slices,
closures, filehandle return, hashref, self-chain, our-array, str, recursion,
values, empty/undef edges) is also byte-identical.

THREE DESIGN DEVIATIONS, each forced by a measurement:

 (1) `:void` DOES NOT SKIP THE COPY.  The design said ":void -> v unchanged
     (nothing consumes it)".  False for PCL: the void regime binds *wantarray*
     to :void around a whole DISCARDED STATEMENT, so an inner call whose value
     IS consumed sees :void too.  Two probe rows fail with the early-out â
     `my $r = \f(); $$r = 10` (emitted `(p-my-= $r (p-backslash (pl-f)))`
     inside the statement's void wrap) and `sub mod { $_[0] = 12 } mod(f())`
     (`(p-void-ctx (pl-mod (pl-f)))`).  :void now takes the SCALAR rule, which
     leaves raw aggregates exactly as they were.

 (2) A VECTOR'S SHAPE IS SEMANTIC â the design's "a FRESH adjustable
     fill-pointer vector (p-flatten-args' shape)" is WRONG and cost the gate
     15 rows before it was found.  PCL distinguishes an ARRAY (adjustable +
     fill pointer; its slots are the values) from a LIST TEMP (the simple
     vector the emitter builds for a comma list, whose aggregate elements are
     still UNFLATTENED and are expanded by the consumer's %p-flatten-list
     walk).  Copying a list temp into an adjustable vector told every consumer
     it was an array, so a nested aggregate became ONE element â a reference.
     `sub steps { qw(x), $_[0]->SUPER::steps }` is Role::Tiny's
     role_application_steps exactly, so `foreach my $step (â¦)` yielded
     ARRAY(0x1) and EVERY Moo role application died (Pl/t/moo-01.t 15/15 red).
     %p-leavesub-vector now mirrors array-has-fill-pointer-p /
     adjustable-array-p and leaves nested aggregates to the consumer.

 (3) A GENUINE DUALVAR CARRIES ITS IDENTITY ON THE BOX, and the accident the
     design asked to remove was LOAD-BEARING.  p-return-value's container arm
     tested `(vectorp v)`; a CL string IS a vector, so `$!` and
     `Scalar::Util::dualvar(42,"forty-two")` rode out of it BOXED â keeping
     both halves â purely by accident.  Adding the honest `(not (stringp v))`
     dropped the numeric half and Pl/t/errno-01.t rows 16-19 failed.  Routed
     through the runtime's OWN single reading and copier (%pcl-dualvar-p /
     %p-dualvar-copy, the pair the raw-element storage rule already uses), in
     p-return-value AND in %p-leavesub-scalar.

 (3b) ONE ADDITION beyond the design, with the measurement: the design said a
     raw hash-table needs nothing because "the consumer flattens k/v fresh".
     Measured false â p-flatten-args hands out %p-hash-elem-cell ALIASES for
     the value half (and must: `f(%h)` lets the callee write $_[1] through), so
     `my %h=(a=>1); sub fh { %h } for my $v (fh()) { $v='W' if $v eq '1' }`
     wrote W into %h where perl leaves it alone.  A non-blessed, non-marker
     hash-table is copied into a fresh table of the SAME TYPE (not flattened),
     so no consumer sees a shape change.

COST (the USER's bar).  %p-leavesub is INLINE with the RAW arm first: a raw
return is already a copy, so the whole rule is one struct typep + one special
read with NO call.  Out of line and list-first it cost 4-9 % on the call-heavy
rows, so the shape matters.
  Instrument: interleaved runtime A/B (BENCH_RT_B), best-of-5, FIVE runs, this
  runtime vs the same runtime with %p-leavesub short-circuited.  Then the
  CONTROL that makes the numbers readable: the same A/B with side B a
  BYTE-IDENTICAL COPY of the runtime reports symref +14.2 % and intloop=
  -5.0 % with a consistent sign across three runs.  So the consistent-sign
  method has a per-row bias of +-5 % on this box (+-15 % for symref) and
  nothing smaller is interpretable.
  Against that floor, the ONLY row with a mechanism is ovlsub ~ -4 % (two
  blessed-box mortalcopies per iteration â exactly perl's own cost).  Every row
  the bar names is inside the control band: gcdrec -1.9, collatz -0.4,
  intloop+= -2.6, intloop= -0.7, arrhash -0.2, symref -4.7 (control +14.2).
  fib(27)x reads A FASTER in all five runs (+3.1 %), which is causally
  impossible and is the same artifact.
  Branch-vs-main ABSOLUTES (both full tables, same machine, PCL seconds):
  every row within +-3 % except intloop= +6.1 %, whose hot loop contains no sub
  call at all.  ovlsub 0.1313 -> 0.1335 (+1.7 %), symref 0.0310 -> 0.0310,
  gcdrec 0.0923 -> 0.0949, fib 0.4006 -> 0.4079.
  NO compile-time escape (the _sub_return_facts Kind-A entry) was needed.

                  pclxs xs rows red (xs-01 5, xs-02 4, xs-03 4).
  corpus-diff     49 of 111 files differ; 271 hunks, and EVERY hunk is exactly

                  `: lvalue`: op/sub_lval.t 54/47 -> 31/64 (23 rows;
                  get_lex/get_st/id/id1/inc are all `: lvalue`, lines 34-38),
                  op/kvaslice.t 24/14 -> 23/15 and op/kvhslice.t 20/18 ->
                  19/19 (both `sub foo:lvalue{ %a[@i] }; $_++ foreach foo()`).
                  Attributed by a base-worktree (a8b4043) run of the same four

                  BY ROW into baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv with the cause.

  guards          NEW Pl/t/return-copy-01.t â the 38-row battery as FOUR
                  programs (4 SBCL launches, 1.54 s wall) plus two

                  p-sort-cmp and eval { } keep the bare catch.

=== s464b RESULT (Opus, 2026-09-02) â THE #964 RESIDUE, second commit on the same branch (rebased onto main 8a83f3e; s464a is 551202b). ===

FABLE'S FINDING, reproduced first: a raw aggregate ELEMENT of a returned list
temp was passed through uncopied, so the consumer's flatten walk aliased the
callee's array.  Pre-existing on main and inside #964's rule.

  my @a=(1,2,3); my @b=(4,5);
  sub nest_a  { (0, @a) }   for (nest_a())  { $_ = 'W' }   perl 1 2 3      was W W W
  sub two_arr { (@a, @b) }  for (two_arr()) { $_ = 'W' }   perl 1 2 3|4 5  was W W W|W W

FIX â two steps, and the second is the one the fix shape did not predict:

 (1) The per-element rule of %p-leavesub-vector is now %p-leavesub-element ("a
     box -> %p-leavesub-scalar; anything else -> %p-leavesub-aggregate"), the
     shape Fable specified.  %p-leavesub-vector and %p-leavesub-aggregate are
     therefore mutually recursive (finite: a Perl list's nesting is), with a
     forward `(declaim (ftype (function (t) t) %p-leavesub-aggregate))`.

 (2) THAT ALONE DID NOT FIX EITHER ROW.  The emitter does not put a bare vector
     in the slot: `sub nest_a { (0, @a) }` lowers to
     `(if *wantarray* (vector 0 (p-flatten @a)) â¦)`, and `(p-flatten @a)` is a
     `p-flatten-marker` STRUCT around the LIVE array â a deferred flatten, not
     an aggregate value.  %p-leavesub-aggregate gained a marker arm that
     rebuilds the marker around the copied array, so the deferral survives and
     only the storage changes.  (This is why `sub { @a }` and `return (@a, 9)`
     were already right: the first hands over the array itself, the second is
     flattened by p-return before the frame sees it.)

Copying SAME-SHAPE is not flattening: the element stays ONE element and the
consumer still flattens it, so the s464a Role::Tiny finding is untouched â
`Pl/t/moo-01.t` re-run explicitly and green, and the `nest2.pl` probe
(`sub steps { qw(x), $_[0]->SUPER::steps }`) still yields x|a|b.

=== s464aw (round 22, 2026-09-02): THE SIBLING RULE #987 IS SHIPPED.

This task's design named it and scoped it out ("perl copies at BOTH sub and
eval-BLOCK exit -- pp_leavesub / pp_leaveeval -- and NOT at `do { }`: file
it").  `%p-leavesub` now also wraps the `catch :p-return` at `p-eval-block`
and at the string eval, closing eight probe rows; `do { }` needed no
exclusion, having no catch of its own.

Nothing in THIS task's machinery changed -- the vector-shape rule, the dualvar
arm, the `:void` rule and the caller's-*wantarray* property all carried over
untouched, which is the payoff of having written the rule once.  The remaining
frames stay bare by design: `p-sort-cmp` (numified value) and `p-goto-sub`
(the target runs its own frame).
subject: SILENT WRONG: an ORDINARY sub that returns a scalar VARIABLE returns its BOX, so every aliasing consumer (foreach, map/grep $_, \f(), an @_-writing callee) writes into the caller's variable -- perl returns a COPY unless the sub is :lvalue
